items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: well Maurice Hines, the other Hines brother, he introduced me to my future wife. He became good friends.

ctx.x: The fighter. And even Keter Betts and Houston [Person] were talking about, “Man when he would fight, everyone, it was like that was a rallying point. It was like well they could kick us down but we’ve got the best athletes and we’ve got the best artists. And so we saw, when I was a kid, Leotyne Price, and we were so proud. It was like when we walked

into the hall, my mother and father’s head just went a little bit higher. Because they were saying she’s ours. This is something that we’re proud of. And you can oppress us in all these other kinds of ways. But we’ve got these great artists, like Lena Horne they were so proud of, and they took me to see her. They took me to see Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald twice, took me to see Duke Ellington three times, Count Basie I went a couple of times, then my father, there was this hall that would always have him, he…

my new guys I like, he’s got a little website, I can order his records, I don’t even have to go through a distributor. Go to the website, I can order through the website, he’ll send me a good copy of it, I can read all about it and where his next gig is on the web. See it’s interesting, we’re going to be able to bypass a lot of things as time goes on. So I think it would be important for a college to teach that to young people as well as the other skills. Integrate new things into it.
